requirements.statement: Each <svg> element that carries information has role="img".

citations.quote: Chaque image vectorielle (balise `<svg>`) porteuse d’information, vérifie-t-elle ces conditions ?
Si ce n’est pas le cas, le test est invalidé.

routes.statement: The <svg> element has the attribute role="img".

citations.quote: La balise `<svg>` possède un attribut WAI-ARIA `role="img"` ;

requirements.statement: Each <svg> element that carries information has a text alternative.

citations.quote: La balise `<svg>` a une alternative textuelle.
vérifier que l’élément `<svg>` est pourvu au moins d’une alternative textuelle parmi les suivantes :

routes.statement: The content of a <title> element of the <svg> gives the alternative.
A passage of text is associated with the <svg> through aria-labelledby.

citations.quote: Passage de texte associé via l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-labelledby` ;

routes.statement: The <svg> element's aria-label attribute gives the alternative.
The alternative is present in a <text> element of the <svg>, visible or not.

citations.quote: pour les images vectorielles (balise <svg>) l’alternative textuelle pourrait se trouver aussi présente dans une balise <title> ou dans une balise <text> que cette dernière balise soit ou non visible

exceptions.statement: An image that is the only content of a link has the link's text as its alternative, and the glossary sends that alternative to the Links theme.

citations.quote: lorsque l’image est le seul contenu d’un lien, son alternative est l’intitulé du lien. Dans ce cas, l’alternative de l’image devrait être évaluée avec la thématique « Liens ».

exceptions.statement: An <svg> that is the only content of a <button> has the button's text as its alternative, and the glossary sends it to the Forms or Scripts theme.

rationale.text: The wording asks two conditions of each <svg> that carries information, and both must hold: the methodology invalidates the test as soon as role="img" is missing, before it looks for an alternative. So the entry has two requirements. The alternative has the three sources the methodology lists, a <title> element, aria-labelledby and aria-label, and a fourth from the glossary: a <text> element, visible or not. The glossary notes on images alone in a link or a <button> are exceptions to the alternative only; they say where the image's alternative is evaluated and nothing about its role. Whether an <svg> carries information is judgment, and it decides whether either requirement applies. A missing role or a missing alternative proves nothing on its own: the <svg> may be decorative, and then this test does not apply to it. An <svg> with a <title> but no role is no better a witness, since drawing tools leave <title> elements in decorative pictures. So no fault proves failure, and the entry is none. axe's svg-img-alt examines only elements that already have role img or image (or a graphics role) inside SVG, so it never looks at an <svg> without the role and never examines the first requirement. For the second, it checks a direct <title> child, aria-label and aria-labelledby, but not <text> elements, so its fault may fall on an <svg> that meets the test through <text>, on a decorative one, or on the only content of a link. It also accepts a non-empty title attribute, which the methodology does not list and the glossary order does not give for <svg>, so its clean result proves nothing. Its link is partial and evidence only. Applicability is judgment: it depends on which <svg> elements carry information. Needs is empty: the methodology reads elements and attributes.
